steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C).
Mix vegetable oil, dressing mix, dill weed, lemon pepper, and garlic powder together in a large bowl.
Add oyster crackers; toss to coat. Spread evenly on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until lightly browned, 15 to 20 minutes; stir gently after 10 minutes of baking.
Remove from the oven and allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Ranch Oyster Crackers
raw_recipe.description: These oyster crackers are seasoned with ranch dressing mix, dill, lemon pepper, and garlic powder for an easy-to-make and easy-to-eat party snack.

video.description: Make the perfect snack for kids or adults with this quick-and-easy recipe. In this video, learn how to make ranch oyster crackers using ranch seasoning, oil, dill, lemon pepper, and garlic powder. Take all of those ingredients and mix them together with a pack of oyster crackers. Put them on a pan and into the oven for 20 minutes at 250 degrees. Enjoy these tangy and savory bite sized crackers on their own or with a cocktail in hand.

review.reviewBody: very quick and easy to put together and make. tasty too! be sure to stir them after ten minutes and "drain" evenly on paper towels to take away some of the greasy-ness.

These bring back so many memories of my childhood and my Aunt Gayle making them. I decided to give it a try. It didn't disappoint. I did a double batch so I bought two 9oz bags of oyster crackers and doubled the spices + oil. (I used "salt-free lemon pepper"). However, I made the two batches individually. I laid out a piece of foil on the first baking sheet and spread those out. The first batch started baking and I mixed every 5 minutes or so for 20 min. While that was cooking, I started the second batch and cooked the same amount of time. Some reviewers indicated that they were too salty, so before I transferred them from the baking sheet, I shook the sheet for a few minutes to remove excess salt, and then poured into a holiday container (then repeated for the second batch). Two thumbs up from both of my girls. One of them even said "I love my mama's cooking!"

The vegetable oil can be overwhelming so I replaced it with Orville Redenbacher's butter flavored popcorn oil. Heat it on the stove on medium low heat until warm and add all the seasonings. Stir and heat until mostly dissolved before pouring over the oyster crackers.

I would leave the amount of crackers as recipe has it but double all other ingredients for more flavor and coverage. I found using a plastic grocery bag makes it much easier to shake and cover the crackers better before baking

Made it with 18 oz. crackers (2 - 9oz. packages Premium Oyster Crackers). One cup oil, 2.5 tsps. lemon pepper, 2.5 tsps. dill weed, 2.5 tsps. garlic powder, 1 package Hidden Valley Ranch dry mix. I mix it all, then put on paper towels on cookie sheet to dry, no baking. Yummy!

Delicious and addictive! If you want snack that tastes like this but is better for you, you can replace the oyster crackers with 2 or 3 cans (depending on how strong you like your flavors) drained, rinsed and dried garbanzo beans. Dry roast the beans 10 min @ 425F, shake, 10 min, mix with seasonings, back in the oven for 10 min, shake, 10 min, done. Just as delicious, but fewer carbs and more protein and fiber.

My dear departed neighbor lady turned me on to these years ago. However, she (and now I) do it a little differently. Instead of oil, use spray butter and spritz the tops. Don't skimp on the dressing. A touch of sea salt and garlic sprinkled on top is all that's needed. No need to stir them when in the oven.

I found some crushed red pepper flavored oyster crackers at Kroger earlier in the week, and thay make a wonderful addition to the plain ones with just ranch dressing. Mix erm 50/50 with the plain ones, and you'll be impressed/

Don’t skimp on the “optional” ingredients. I see comments calling this recipe bland, and the only thing I can think is that they’re skimping on ingredients. This is identical to my mom’s recipe, but she doesn’t use lemon pepper. I made 1 batch with it and one without and did a blind taste test with my daughter and she prefers the ones with lemon pepper. Also, bake for 10 mins, stir & bake for 10mins more. The low/slow baking really makes the flavors soak into the crackers.

I make these all the time with regular saltines. First time making them with oyster crackers. I omitted the LP and added red pepper flakes instead. I checked this recipe to see if the oil ratio was correct. I also put them under the broiler to brown them a bit more after the 20 minutes. Thank you for posting! 😊

I made these so my family could have a tasty snack. I did follow the recipe exactly. I used premium oyster crackers instead of store brand. While shopping i noticed the store brand crackers had salt on them so that's why I chose the premium. They were rather salty but very yummy. Before making i skimmed a few reviews and noticed that one suggested to cool on paper towels. That this would help to soak up the grease. Instead of vegetable oil I opted to use olive oil and they were not greasy at all.
Sometimes I replace some of the oil with melted unsalted butter (maybe 2 TBS or so). I love using these as croutons on my salad with home made ranch dressing
These are delicious and addictive.
My grandkids definitely love this. Make it regularly at our house. I measure with my heart not my utensils with this recipe.
The classic recipe that I was looking for.
I omitted the lemon pepper and dill but added cayenne. Big hit at our house and so easy!
Yumm! It is so tangy and delicous!
Only problem is..i can't stop eating them!! So good!!
All time family favorite. Easy to prepare and great taste for a fraction of the price of store bought items.
I like to use mini saltines instead of oyster crackers, sometimes.
This is a great great recipe!
